newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka gets $10 mln U.S. soft loan for rice.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka gets $10 mln U.S. soft loan for rice.

text.p: The United States on Monday signed an agreement to provide a soft loan of $10 million to Sri Lanka to buy about 28,000 tonnes of rice this year, the U.S. embassy said.

The 1996 P.L.-480 Title 1 agreement allows Sri Lanka 30 years to repay the loan after a five-year grace period, an embassy statement said. Annual interest will be three percent in the first seven years and four percent thereafter.
The U.S. has already provided another $10 million soft loan to the Indian Ocean island as part of its food aid programme so far this year, it said.
Under the food aid programme, Sri Lanka can also import about 47,000 tonnes of wheat, representing about five percent of its annual wheat imports, the statement said.
Sri Lanka has received more than $880 million of food under the P.L.-480 programme since 1956, it said.
The government has said Sri Lanka needs to import up to 500,000 tonnes of rice by the end of this year to meet an anticipated crop shortfall caused by drought and rising demand.
The private sector has already imported more than 100,000 tonnes in the first seven months of this year.
